result.reason: All three items together present Rav Pappa's explanation of why 'lapar' is needed — to package the yoteret v'shetei kelayot (derived only by hekesh in the par helam davar) as if explicitly written there, so it can be re-exported to the se'irei avoda zara without violating the rule against davar halamed b'hekesh chozer u'melamed b'hekesh — which is precisely what the 'Packaging Exports' prose section describes.
The passage is the opening citation of the baraita in support of Rav Pappa (tanya kevatei de-Rav Pappa), which is precisely what the 'Baraita Parsing' section's prose describes as its starting point.

All six items form a continuous chain about why the verse 'chatatam asher shagu' was necessary beyond the earlier ribui, Rav Pappa's answer about the yoteret v'shetei haklayot, Rav Huna's challenge, and the tannaitic resolution — precisely the content described in the 'Link Source Debate' prose, which covers all these elements including the tannaitic dispute at the end.

Both items are the school of Rabbi Yishmael's midrashic teachings explaining why the par helam davar shel tzibbur omits the yoteret v'shetei haklayot and the word 'kodesh' with parochet, which is precisely what the 'Midrashic Omissions' prose describes in detail.

The passage quotes the Menachos mishna about piggul in the kometz but not the levona (or vice versa) and Rabbi Meir's ruling, which is precisely what the 'Menachos Comparison' prose section describes and analyzes.

The passage quotes the Rabbis' ruling that there is no karet unless piggul intention accompanies the entire matir, which is precisely the chachamim's position ('ein bo karet ad she'yefagel b'chol hamatir') discussed in the Menachos Comparison prose.

The passage presents Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish's reframing of Rabbi Meir's position based on the principle 'kol ha'oseh al da'as rishona hu oseh,' which is precisely what the 'Da'as Rishona Principle' section's prose discusses.

All 8 items form a continuous chain discussing the reconciliation of the mishna's language (ke-tiknan/shelo ke-tiknan) with the rabbanan's position, covering Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak's reinterpretation, Rava's chutz limkomo reading, Rav Ashi's shelo lishmo reading, and the gemara's final resolution via parallel framing — exactly matching the 'Rava Reconciliation' section's prose description.

All three items constitute the baraita citation and the gemara's immediate objection drawn from it — exactly what the 'Braiata Explicit' prose describes: the distinction between outer and inner altar blood applications, the forty-three/eleven counts, Rabbi Meir vs. Rabbis on piggul at any stage, and the gemara's pointed conclusion that this contradicts Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish's reading of Rabbi Meir.
